name: Foundations and Applications of Machine Learning in Photonics
description: Introduction to photonics: Maxwell’s equations, guided-wave devices, coupled-mode theory, photonic integrated circuits, and numerical modeling methods (FDTD, FEM). Foundations of machine learning: supervised and unsupervised learning, regression, classification, clustering, dimensionality reduction, neural networks, deep learning, optimization, and reinforcement learning. Machine learning for photonic device modeling: inverse design, surrogate models, gratings, resonators, photonic crystals, metasurfaces, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, and generative models. ML for photonic sensing and signal processing: spectral demodulation, multiparameter calibration, noise suppression, nonlinear sensing, and optical communication. Advanced topics: physics informed neural networks, hybrid physics ML frameworks, quantum photonics, non Hermitian systems, explainability, and case studies.
